text:
alex: paging — latency alerts for inference-prod P95 spiking to 3.2s, errors small but tail latency is awful. customer impact: slow responses for streaming and non-streaming requests. seen across models.
ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2149993 — latency spike in inference-prod. Paging primary oncall: alex.
alex: quick TL;DR from initial checks: queue depth jumped, HPA didn't immediately scale, GPU pool showing high allocation and lots of warmup churn. attaching initial metrics.
alex: metrics snapshot: queue_depth=1420, inflight=980, avg_warmup_time=18s, gpu_pool_util=94%.
dan: on it, joining. any customer-reported errors or just latency?
alex: mostly timeouts and long tails. a few clients reported stalled streams. no 5xx spike.
maria: tagging visibility — I'm day shift, can take handoff once we have mitigation plan.
jess: I see burst of cold-starts in the warmup logs matching the queue surge. warmup pod churn high because node pod evictions triggered reschedules.
alex: adding raw log excerpt: ```
[2026-03-15T09:02:14Z] warmup: pod-start id=wm-xyz status=init
[2026-03-15T09:02:32Z] warmup: pod-ready id=wm-xyz kvcache-miss
[2026-03-15T09:03:01Z] request: queued id=req-7f; reason=pool-saturated
[2026-03-15T09:03:30Z] request: dequeue id=req-7f; wait=116s
```
alex: hypothesis 1: HPA failed to scale quickly because metrics were delayed or HPA threshold configured too low vs surge. hypothesis 2: GPU pool saturated because autoscaler didn't spin up new GPU nodes fast enough (cloud warmup delay). hypothesis 3: warmup cancellation + churn causing wasted capacity and increasing queue depth.
dan: running quick HPA check. ```kubectl get hpa inference-svc -n prod -o yaml```
jen: paste of HPA output (trimmed): ```
metrics: - type: Resource   resource: name: cpu target: averageUtilization: 70
status: currentReplicas: 12   desiredReplicas: 12   lastScaleTime: 2026-03-15T08:58:10Z
```
dan: HPA didn't increase because CPU metric didn't cross threshold — requests were queuing at the runtime level not visible to kube cpu metric.
jess: runtime emits queue_depth metric but HPA not configured on it. that's been a known gap.
maria: how fast can we increase dedicated pool manually? can we add GPUs or bump reserved?
alex: mitigation options: 1) increase HPA maxReplicas and switch to request-based custom metric; 2) manually scale the replica count for inference-svc; 3) scale GPU pool nodes (cloud console); 4) enable fallback routing to a smaller/quantized model to drop latency.
dan: I'm manually scaling replicas to 18 now: `kubectl scale deployment inference-svc --replicas=18 -n prod` — doing it because HPA hasn't reacted.
ops-bot: Deploy event: scaled deployment inference-svc -> 18 replicas by dan at 2026-03-15T09:08:12Z.
alex: also opening cloud pool scale request to infra: jess can you raise GPU node count?
jess: on it. raising pool min nodes from 12 -> 16. AWS API call in progress.
jess: cloud response: launch requests submitted, expected warm node availability ~6-7m due to image pull + init.
alex: enabling fallback: shifting 20% traffic to quantized-1b model to reduce tail. `route set traffic inference-prod --model quant-1b --weight 0.2`
dan: traffic shift applied. initial effect: queue_depth dropped from 1420 -> 980 in ~60s. P95 down to 1.6s.
maria: I'm taking over oncall at 09:20. handoff notes: manual scale to 18, GPU pool scale requested, 20% fallback routing in place. still monitoring queue and warmup churn.
alex: adding timeline notes for RCA: - 09:00 sudden traffic spike (client-side batch job) - 09:02 queue depth climb - 09:05 HPA did not scale due to CPU metric blind spot - 09:07 manual scale applied - 09:09 fallback routing reduced tail - 09:15 GPU nodes starting to come up - 09:23 pool warmups stabilizing.
dan: adding logs for hypothesis tracking. logs show many warmup pods reaching ready but with KV cache misses, meaning repeated cold-starts; likely the pod lifecycle is cycling due to node pressure/evictions.
jess: found node term events at ~08:58 causing eviction cascades, cloud provider had preemption window for the autoscaler. attaching event snippet: ```
NodeEvent: ec2-i-0abc Terminated - ScaleDown; timestamp=2026-03-15T08:58:03Z
```
jess: so autoscaler trimmed nodes then burst traffic arrived, leading to insufficient capacity and warmup race.
maria: proposed short-term fixes to add to RCA action items: - add runtime queue_depth as HPA metric - add warmup cache persistence to reduce cold-start cost - increase buffer in node autoscaler scale-down grace period - implement automatic fallback routing when queue_depth > X
dan: agreed. also recommend a runbook change: when queue_depth > 500 and P95 > 1s, trigger immediate manual scale and fallback routing before waiting for HPA.
alex: tagging stakeholders for customer impact postmortem: growth-eng, solutions, accounts. I'll draft initial incident summary once metrics stabilize.
ops-bot: Incident INC-2149993 severity set to SEV3.
maria: leaving final note: system stabilized at 09:25, queue_depth back to 120, P95 ~ 0.9s. closing pager but keeping RCA thread open.
alex: thanks all. will open formal RCA doc and link here. :thumbsup:
incident-bot: Reminder: add timeline, mitigation, root cause, and action items to INC-2149993 within 24h.
